body.p: Now I will tell a tale. Once upon a time there lived three men. It seems, they were brothers. They had reindeer, they fished, they were with the reindeer. They were three, they had no mother. Three ... Three lads lived alone. There was the youngest brother. His name was Bunulya. ... the youngest brother said every time. As for me, I will die soon. His brothers said. How, Bunulya? How will you die? You are not ill! Bunulya says. I will die, evidently, I will die. If I die, let you put caviar and barika into my coffin. His brothers said. Bunulya, calm down! Don't say it in vain, how will you die? You are not ill at all! Well, some days passed. Bunulya cries to his brothers. I will die soon! And they say. How will you die? Bunulya, stop it further! Bunulya said. When I die, let you put me here, this my coffin... so that when I die, I look to my brothers. This Bunulya, as he said, started dying. What will they do then, he died, after all. They made a coffin for him, to put their Bunulya.[ShA:] PunodÊ¼ is an unexpected form, pumodÊ¼ is expected.They put there his body. Maybe three days left, I don't know, after he died. The other brother went out outdoors and said. Something, well, seems to my eyes, to my ears. He said to his elder brother. Bunulya seems. The elder brother said. How will he seem? How will seem and already dead person? He really, really seems! Oh, you lie, how will he seem? Oh my God, don't seem to us the next day! Some more days passed. It's autumn, after all, it's dark. It's a dark time in September. The younger brother again went outdoors. His brother seems again. So he, hear, speaks, hear, laughs. Ha ha, now I with you! He looks to him and laughs. And the caviar is seen in his mouth. The brother got afraid. He said again to his elder brother. My god! That one, it seems, seems to us again. Now he went about again, he laughed. He appears to me with the caviar, the caviar is seen on his teeth. The elder brother said. Calm him down! How ... us? We live alone, so he seems to us. Some days passed, ... passed. He still sees him when he goes out. And he does not bother his elder brother, does not, well. He only frightens his younger brother, like an alive person. He is such, anyway. It will be good if we kill a reindeer for him, in order that he would not bother his brother. His brothers say. We will kill a reindeer for him, what will be then?[ShA:] The inflection of kazanÊ²Ê is unclear. Why does he bother only one of us? We will kill a reindeer for him, so that he will not bother you anymore. And so, the brothers killed a reindeer near his coffin. In order that he would not bother his brother. Some days passed. Once the elder brother went out in the evening. Evidently, he thought: This will be my younger brother. So he started frightening his elder brother. So he laughs there. He frightened his elder brother. He said. What does he do there? He is like an alive. But the elder brother had a lot of intelligence, after all. He thought. Now I will, well, you at some time. If you are really alive, you will be frightened now. And if you are dead, you will not be frightened. You are lying here, after all. You would not frighten your brothers.[ShA:] The strucure of izaxud is unclear;. So ..., frighten us! The brothers killed a reindeer and put it to the deceased.It's d ark in the evening, after all. They both are standing outdoors. The night already fell. So they cried to him. Bunulya, a bear appeared there! He started throwing around your coffin! So the former deceased threw away his coffin, and the pail with the caviar went somewhere topsy-turvy. The dead person cries weeping. Where, where is the bear? The elder brother cries. Bunulya, the bear appeared there! So, they frightened him with a bear. So the brothers gave him a scolding, maybe beat him, maybe somehow else. The elder brother said. And why did you do so with us? As for you, you have enough intelligence to frighten us to such an extent.
